# Self-review

**Correctness — PASS.** The equation is equivalent, with no omitted repeated-variable cases, to the support hypergraph generated by \(u=3x+7y-z\) in \((\mathbb Z/8\mathbb Z)^2\). The exhaustive integer checker enumerates every one of \(64^3\) triples, deduplicates exactly \(31{,}152\) forbidden supports, proves by increasing-order recursion that there are \(12{,}288\) rooted admissible eight-sets and no rooted nine-set, and enumerates all \(1{,}536\) invertible matrices and their rooted orbits. Translation and incidence counting give the unrooted totals. The code was executed from the supplied standalone path and returned `VERIFY_OK`; a separately compiled integer-only C++ version produced the same rooted counts and exact maximum. This is a complete finite proof, not extrapolation from random cases.

**Originality — PASS, with recorded risk.** The primary preprint arXiv:2610.09887v1 treats the same asymmetric equation, but its displayed results concern asymptotic lower bounds, prime-field vector spaces and a different finite cyclic-group equation in its table. The related arXiv:2609.13972v1 concerns large integer sets. Actual exact-object/alias searches of a mathematical-result index and the web identified no covering rank-two four-orbit census. No uniqueness of discovery is inferred merely from search failure. Some full-text portions of both papers were inaccessible; independently indexed or implicit earlier exact counts remain possible.

**Value — PASS.** The base-eight group is structurally singled out by the motivating high-density construction, while rank two is its first noncyclic testing ground. The determination of the exact finite extremal number and complete four-class affine classification supplies a natural extremal invariant, demonstrates saturation of the square-root bound at that rank, and distinguishes inequivalent maximum candidate gadgets for further constructions. It is neither a textbook substitution nor a randomly selected finite slice: the modulus, equation and rank arise from the literature's specific construction. No downstream theorem or asymptotic breakthrough is claimed.

**Closest literature and limitations.** Gyarmati, arXiv:2610.09887v1 (same equation; different quantifiers and finite table); Hametner–Solymosi, arXiv:2609.13972v1 (asymptotic interval constructions). This exact finite calculation is self-contained once the checker is run or its exhaustive recursion is examined. It does not settle any higher-rank extremal exponent. The originality comparison is subject to incomplete access to some primary full texts.

Self-review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.
